_meta.purpose: The complete LP-grading rubric. Every weight, curve, threshold, boundary, and lens that produces a published grade lives HERE — edit this file, the next lp-grades run reflects it, no code change. The cron echoes config_version + file sha into every output so each scored snapshot says which rubric produced it.
laws: Weights within any group must sum to 1.0 — the cron HALTS loudly otherwise (a typo must never silently rescale the world).
A metric with no trustworthy source is null and its weight renormalizes across the remaining metrics — never fabricated.

Strategic judgment does NOT go in this file — it goes in override files ({discovered, override, value, note}, reason required, needs_dao_prop for weighty premiums). This file is the public rubric; overrides are governed exceptions.
This is DRAFT v0.1.0 — every number below is a starting position to argue with, several flagged to open decisions D1–D6 in the spec.

quality_grade._note: Quality = A x B, the 'how good is this pool' grade. C is an OVERLAY (see support_gap), not a component here — spec decision D2.
quality_grade._D1: A .60 / B .40 is the performance-forward draft; owner to confirm or move toward equality.

depth._note: carried from interim grade; log so a 10x depth gap matters more at the thin end

utilization._note: volume/liquidity; 50%/week turnover = 100. Null where no trustworthy volume source (SkeletonSwap) — renormalizes, never faked.

exit_slippage._note: pool-type-aware: XYK exact; PCL/stable score on the <= bound (their true impact is lower by design)

durability_B1._note: rebuilt from the legacy confusion-score factors on token-catalog Stage 2; per-pool = weighted mean of underlyings

asset_class_B2._note: three classes, three fact bases (spec 3.B2). Strategic premiums (e.g. ATOM IBC-hub) are NOT here — they are overrides in asset_value_overrides.json with stated reasons.

ibc_infrastructure._note: modest floor; the strategic role premium comes from governed overrides, by design

native_terra._note: never market-cap scored; the native-stable elevation must remain the most transparently justified weight in the rubric

chain_alignment_B3._D6: generated flow (take_rate x utilization proxy) vs absolute take-rate — draft picks generated flow

support_gap_C._note: OVERLAY, not part of the quality grade (spec D2). Answers 'does it need you'. All comparisons within-bucket by default (D4).

caps._note: a pool that cannot demonstrate depth/utilization must not outrank pools earning full marks on all metrics

confidence._D3: 4-epoch floor for firm grades is the draft; 6 is the stricter option

states._note: new pools are never graded F for lacking history — they publish as state:new, the jump-start candidate list

lenses.label: Best for the chain
lenses.description: The absolute best pools for Terra and its users — quality (A x B), no opportunity weighting.

lenses.label: Needs votes
lenses.description: Deserving and under-supported, within their bucket — where your vote works hardest.

lenses.label: Underdogs
lenses.description: Small pools doing real work with below-median support — the discovery list.

lenses.label: Chain builders
lenses.description: Pools generating the most take-rate flow into chain-owned liquidity.

lenses.label: Trader's choice
lenses.description: Best pools for people actually trading — depth, honest exits, real throughput.

lenses.label: Active projects
lenses.description: Project-bucket pools with the most real activity behind them.

lenses.label: New pools
lenses.description: Too new to grade honestly — the jump-start candidates.

lenses.label: Bribe targets
lenses.description: Quality pools with no pot — a first bribe here has zero competition.

lenses.label: At risk
lenses.description: Near the 1% cliff — staked value stops earning if they slip.

lenses.label: Healthy to enter
lenses.description: The safety view: same quality facts, support-gap de-emphasized — is this a sound pool to LP into?

advisor._note: Parameters for the on-page aDAO Vote Advisor + Bribe Planner (Rev G2). The recommendation is a DETERMINISTIC algorithm over the published grades — every parameter here is public so the output is arguable, never hidden opinion. Council judgment always decides; this is the rubric's answer, not an instruction.

vote._chunk_note: TLA votes allocate in 10% chunks per bucket (weight_bps multiples of 1000). Each bucket gets the wallet's FULL VP, split across that bucket's pools in these chunks.
vote._objective_note: Each 10% chunk goes to the bucket pool with the highest quality x underpaid-ratio, RECOMPUTED after every chunk as our own assigned VP raises the pool's support — so the advisor never piles all chunks on one pool past the point of diminishing need.
vote._cap_note: Diversification cap: no single pool receives more than this share of a bucket's VP, however dominant its marginal need — real voters defend multiple thresholds, and an all-in recommendation would overstate the rubric's confidence. Raise to 10000 to disable.

bribe._note: Budget allocates in unit_usd chunks, greedily by need_score with diminishing returns as a pool's planned pot grows; a placement below min_effective_pot_usd is merged upward rather than dust-split. Candidates: graded pools flagged bribe_target or underpaid.
